messages:
Liam: quick heads-up — after merging the flash-attn adapter (v3-path) into canary we observed a spike in p99 for mid-sequence workloads (~512 tokens). p99 went from ~120ms to ~260ms for the same batch sizes. anyone else seeing this?
Maria: saw it too on canary-1 around 10:03 UTC. throughput (tokens/s) didn't change much but tail latency doubled.
Elaine: linking a quick perf dump from the canary host: ```
2024-06-09T10:03:12Z INFO model=redwood-v3 seq=512 batch=8 kernel=flashattn_v3 alloc_ms=2.3 compute_ms=180.5 sync_ms=70.2 total_ms=252.9
```
Elaine: sync_ms is the suspect here — looks like extra synchronization on the v3 kernel path.
Jon: @Elaine can you paste the runtime flags? batches, workspace policy, kernel fallback policy?
Elaine: flags: `--batch-max=32 --adaptive-workspace=on --kernel-priority=flashattn_v3,flashattn_v2,gemm` and `--kv-cache=shared`.
Liam: interesting — we had the priority order changed in the adapter RFC to prefer v3 for midseq, with a tiny workspace margin. maybe the allocator is fragmenting and causing extra cuda syncs.
infra-bot: Deploy canary-1: flash-adapter-v3 rolled to nodepool-a (3/3).
Maria: quick experiment idea: force kernel order to v2 first on canary and see tail latency. small change in runtime config, no deploy.
Jon: did a local repro with the model and a synthetic trace: v3 shows repeated `cudaEventSynchronize` calls in the kernel wrapper on midseq. v2 doesn't.
SRE Bot: Note: increased p99 observed correlated with GPU occupancy dip from ~85% to ~60% in the same windows.
Kevin: hypotheses: 1) v3 uses sharded workspace layout that triggers a fallback margin check causing host->device barriers; 2) asynchronous launch ordering gets serialized when workspace allocs fail and we fall back to a safe path; 3) a cache flush on certain token boundary.
Liam: actionable steps: (A) run canary with `--kernel-priority=flashattn_v2,flashattn_v3` for 1h, (B) enable kernel-telemetry (per-invocation timings + sync points), (C) try bumping workspace pool by +10% to see if frag mitigates.
Maria: I've queued (A) now on canary-1 for 30m window. will report.
Elaine: added a quick telemetry patch that logs `pre_launch_alloc_ns`, `launch_ns`, `post_sync_ns` — landing to canary-trace.
Jon: if allocator fragmentation is the issue we might see more OOM-retries in the logs; search for `alloc_failed` or `workspace_realloc`.
Elaine: saw a few `workspace_realloc` warnings right before the spikes. sample: `WARN workspace_realloc model=redwood-v3 seq=512 want=12.3MB avail=9.8MB`
Kevin: sounds consistent. patch proposal: make the allocator prefer contiguous precommit for midseq kernels or fall back to v2 without a sync when realloc would be required. tradeoff: might use slightly more memory.
Liam: +1 to probe memory margin change first. Maria — results?
Maria: after switching priority to v2-first, p99 dropped back to ~130ms (close to baseline). throughput unchanged. will keep it running another 10m.
SRE Bot: Canary window complete (30m). p99 aggregate: baseline 118ms, canary-v3-priority 248ms, canary-v2-first 132ms.
Jon: confirms behavioral difference. Next steps: (1) gather stack traces around alloc path in v3 kernel, (2) add a soft pre-reserve in workspace allocator for sequences >= 384, (3) consider tuning kernel selection heuristic to check `workspace_saturation_ratio` before preferring v3.
Kevin: I'll draft the tiny allocator PR for pre-reserve and a flag `--workspace-headroom=percent`. we can roll it to canary by EOD.
Liam: thanks everyone. let's keep this thread for follow-ups; if Maria's longer run stays green we'll plan a small rollback of the v3-first policy and iterate on the allocator PR. :thumbsup:
